_comment: Labelled prompt set for `fit-token-probe`. Fits a linear direction over canvas hidden state that separates 'about to emit CODE' from 'about to emit PROSE'. NOT model-specific: re-run the fit on any checkpoint and the probe is regenerated in a few minutes. Class order matters — class_names[0] is the NEGATIVE side of the direction, class_names[1] the positive.
_comment_layer: Default 9. Measured on this spec: L6 acc 1.000/effect 2.75, L9 1.000/2.59, L29 0.977/0.97 — so L6 is marginally the strongest for TASK INTENT (what was asked). L9 is chosen instead because PLAN records that tracking the CURRENT emitted mode (trailing committed content, which is what token colouring needs) is best at L9/L29, and L9 gives up almost nothing on intent. Re-fit with --layer to compare on your own checkpoint; compare on EFFECT SIZE, not accuracy, which saturates.
_comment_design: Three deliberate controls, each of which killed a plausible-but-wrong probe during development (see PLAN): (1) HARD NEGATIVES — prose densely about programming (compilers, garbage collection, recursion), so the probe cannot win by spotting technical vocabulary; (2) VERB CONTROL — prose prompts that say 'Write' and code prompts that never do, so it cannot key on the instruction verb; (3) FORMAT VARIANTS — fenced/markdown requests on both sides, so it tracks content type rather than output format. Adding samples is safe; REMOVING a control silently weakens the probe in a way the reported accuracy will not reveal.
